content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Understand the concept of sustainable development

is the protection and preservation of natural resources and biodiversity. As human impacts on ecosystems increase, conservation becomes more important for maintaining healthy ecosystems and ensuring resources for future generations.
Right to exist for all species
The variety of living organisms in an area
Climate change may shift suitable areas
Development that meets present needs without compromising future generations
Restoring natural processes and reintroducing species
Conservation means leaving nature completely alone
Modern zoos contribute significantly to conservation
Conservation is only about rare species
It means development that can continue long-term
Protection of natural resources and biodiversity
Meeting needs without compromising the future
Conservation protects biodiversity and natural resources
Biodiversity includes genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity
In-situ: protecting species in their natural habitat (parks, reserves)
Ex-situ: protecting species outside habitat (zoos, seed banks)
Both approaches have advantages and disadvantages
Sustainable development balances present and future needs
Sustainable fishing uses quotas, mesh sizes, and closed seasons
International cooperation essential for global conservation
